title: Zygote, Forking, and Application Process Creation Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies zygote, forking, and application process creation?
options: Treat Zygote as a preinitialised runtime parent whose child is security-specialised before the app entry point runs.
questions.answer: Treat Zygote as a preinitialised runtime parent whose child is security-specialised before the app entry point runs.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: Zygote forks a copy of the previously running instance of the requested application.
questions.explanation: Describing Zygote as a template containing a fully initialized copy of each app incorrectly implies that application objects and user state exist before the fork.

questions.prompt: Why does Zygote preload common runtime state?
questions.answer: Forked children can reuse clean copy-on-write pages and avoid repeating part of runtime initialization.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
